{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABblXhbA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhFJE6A", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 36, "title": "Redesign WebRTL UI as a clean three-pane RTL development workspace", "body": "## Problem

The WebRTL browser app has accumulated project controls, a large text editor, compiler messages, simulation output and generic Fast/Debug controls in a mostly vertical document flow. The approved UI concept (WebRTL layout mockup from the 2026-11-01 design discussion) instead presents a **clean, desktop IDE-style workspace** where editing is central, project navigation is left, simulation is right, diagnostics are below, and frequent actions are in one compact toolbar.

This is a **UI/UX and layout implementation task**, not a new RTL simulation or SNES-emulation feature. Apply the canonical principles in [README.md#uiux](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/blob/main/README.md#uiux):

1. **Keep it simple:** essential controls and information only.
2. **Show, don't tell:** use layout, spacing and hierarchy instead of long visible explanations.
3. **Intuitive and predictable:** stable placement, familiar controls and no unexpected workflow interruptions.

Preserve labels, accessibility, diagnostics, warnings and destructive-action safeguards.

## Expected outcome

Implement the approved **light-theme, blue-accent WebRTL IDE workspace** with this arrangement:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ WebRTL  [Example ▾] [Compile] [Run] [Pause] [Step] [Reset] [Fast|Debug] ● │
├───────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┤
│ PROJECT       │ EDITOR                        │ SIMULATION                 │
│ Top module    │ [file-a.v][file-b.v][+]       │ [Output / I/O / Signals]  │
│ Files         │                               │ Frame / value / timeline   │
│ Add / import  │    editable RTL source        │ Inputs and signal values  │
│ Examples      │                               │ Debug condition / inspect │
│               │                               ├────────────────────────────┤
│               │                               │ DIAGNOSTICS / TRACE       │
│               │                               │ compile / errors / logs   │
└───────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┘
```

Preserve the mockup's **three principal work areas plus a compact bottom detail panel**, but interpret its decorative example content as illustrative, not mandatory product functionality. In particular, do not invent a RISC-V core, nested project directories, source-line breakpoints, arbitrary SVG waveforms or build scripts just to imitate the pictured labels. WebRTL currently supports flat `.v` project files, named board interfaces and a bounded sampled-signal Debug condition/history.

## Layout and interactions

### Top toolbar: frequent actions

- Show WebRTL identity and an example selector; keep **Compile, Run, Pause, Step, Reset**, **Fast / Debug** selection, and simulation/status indication in a compact, predictable header.
- Keep compile/busy/progress/failure states accessible and legible. Only enable valid controls; preserve pause-at-completed-batch semantics and live-state Fast↔Debug handoff.
- Put less-frequent configuration (HDL frontend, output interface, clock rate) in an easy-to-find but secondary project/simulation area, without burying critical controls.

### Left sidebar: project navigation

- Put top-module selection and the **current project's actual flat source files** here, with a clear active file; provide Add, Import, Rename and Remove actions.
- Present bundled examples (including generic RAM, counters, video/audio, CPU/bus, BG1 and experimental SNES) without dominating the editor. Preserve **“Load example replaces project”** intent and the existing file/source constraints.
- File switching must preserve per-file unsaved in-memory edits; top module, frontend, and output-interface changes retain current invalidation/recompile semantics.
- Use real file names and capabilities rather than pretending nested folders or unsupported `.sv` imports exist.

### Center: source editor as the primary area

- Make the editable RTL source the largest, most prominent region, with clear file tabs or an equivalent compact switcher for the existing multi-file project.
- Maintain source text, cursor/focus, copy/paste, keyboard navigation and readable monospaced content. Syntax coloring/line numbers are welcome only if implemented genuinely without disrupting existing compilation, accessibility or editor input.
- Provide simple empty/loading/compile-error states rather than covering the editing surface with instructional prose.

### Right: simulation and debugging context

- Collect actual RTL result/Canvas, status/time, generic I/O values and relevant controls in one right-side area. Show board-specific SNES cartridge loading/controller help only when SNES is selected; show audio state only when applicable.
- Fast mode primarily shows the actual output and concise runtime state. Debug mode progressively reveals **actual** hierarchical signal/RAM inspection, input controls, supported value/change/edge stop condition, and a **bounded timeline/waveform or clear sampled-history view** derived from real captured data (max 256 clocks currently).
- The mockup's visual “Breakpoints” and waveforms are conceptual. Do not display fictitious source-line breakpoint support or prerecorded signals; label existing capabilities accurately (e.g. Signal condition). If a waveform view is built, it must reflect real selected-signal samples and clock gaps.
- Preserve the current CPU bus trace capability, generic board behavior, SNES Canvas focus and keyboard/gamepad handling, Web Audio unlock, and media lifecycle/reset behavior.

### Bottom: diagnostics and optional details

- Use a compact tabbed/lower section for compiler progress/diagnostics/errors and other genuinely available detail (e.g. trace, signal history). Keep important compilation failures immediately discoverable and announced; do not require hunting for a hidden tab to learn why compilation failed.
- Avoid duplicating the same large signal/trace table in both the right and bottom areas; use one coherent location per concern.
- Prefer progressive disclosure to permanently expanded text and redundant controls.

### Layout adaptation

- At wide desktop widths, maintain the **left navigation / large editor / right simulation** visual hierarchy, consistent spacing, restrained borders/shadows and blue primary actions.
- At narrower widths, collapse/reflow panes or show accessible region tabs so the editor and simulation remain usable without tiny unreadable columns or whole-page horizontal overflow. Do not hide Run/Pause/Compile or critical errors.
- Keep sizes reasonable, scroll *within* panes when appropriate, and retain keyboard access, visible focus, semantic labels, announcements and sufficient contrast.

## Preserve existing WebRTL functionality

This is a **presentation/workflow redesign on top of existing behavior**. Do not regress browser-only compilation with Yosys/Slang/Clang, multi-file project editing, output interface/port validation, video/audio, SNES cartridge import, or Fast/Debug pause-and-resume. Reuse existing `web/index.html`, `web/style.css` and `web/app.js` structure where practical; avoid adding a large UI framework or unrelated simulator changes.

The separate trusted-local UI must still work: the shared HTML/CSS/JS currently serves both browser and local modes. Do not expose browser-only controls in local mode or break its counter workflow.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] At desktop size (~1440×900), the workspace visibly matches the approved **toolbar + left project sidebar + central editor + right simulation + lower diagnostics** composition; the editor clearly gets the most space. The finished UI uses the existing application, not a static illustration.
- [ ] At a narrower desktop/tablet width (~768px), main tasks remain reachable without illegible three-column compression or page-level horizontal overflow; headings, controls, editor and messages remain accessible.
- [ ] Existing bundled examples and relevant board-specific controls are available, with no fake example, fake debugger feature, fake generated waveform, or nonfunctional decorative action.
- [ ] Project add/import/rename/remove/file-switch/top-module/frontend/output-interface operations preserve data and exact source/compile invalidation behavior. Loading an example still clearly communicates replacement.
- [ ] Compile success/progress/errors and Run/Pause/Step/Reset work via the existing real circuit runtime; tests exercise Fast→Pause→Debug→inspect/condition→Fast with retained state and no unintended extra clock/reset.
- [ ] Generic output, Canvas video, PCM/Web Audio and SNES cartridge/input controls appear in their appropriate context and retain expected behavior. Media controls and keyboard focus must not be broken by panel/tab switching.
- [ ] Automated browser layout/interaction checks cover a representative wide/narrow viewport and visible critical state/error UI, plus focused existing browser regressions. Prefer robust DOM/layout assertions and targeted screenshots; avoid subjective human-only signoff or expensive unrelated full SNES corpus reruns.
- [ ] README or focused documentation briefly explains the new workspace and reflects the three existing UI/UX principles without adding a duplicate design system or a new set of principles.

## Not in scope

- A full Monaco/VS Code clone, arbitrary folder support, new file types, a new HDL compiler, new SNES hardware features, true source-line breakpoints, unlimited waveform recording, or unrelated runtime optimization.
- Treating the concept screenshot's decorative simulated values, extra example names or unsupported panes as authoritative requirements.
- Requiring visual approval by a human as the only acceptance check.

## Verification

Use [the repository's development/testing guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/webrtl/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and the established Fast PR smoke plus focused browser tests. Any required live GitHub Pages verification (layout and basic project/compile/run behavior at the deployed commit) is **post-merge only**, not a pre-merge gate.

## Related

- #24 — canonical three UI/UX principles
- #32 — generic Fast / Debug runtime
- #34 — fast development CI
- #3 — general-purpose WebRTL vision
